outcome: respiratory function tests (FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, PEF, MEF75, MEF50, MEF25, MEF25-75)
atopy conditions (fx5, phadiatope, total IgE levels, skin tests)
cohort: The study included 27 preterm infants (hospitalized in NICU for prematurity and treated with aminophylline or caffeine for apnea) and 26 healthy control children, all aged 4-6 years.
finding: Preterm infants treated with aminophylline or caffeine did not have a higher risk of atopy and had similar respiratory function tests compared to healthy infants at 4-6 years old, though FEV1 values were higher in preterm infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
